Subject: Acme POC - initial recap & next steps

Hi John —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the POC kick-off: 

Recap:
- Main objective: validate Redwood can reduce per-token cost for Acme's customer-facing summarization pipelines while meeting 95th percentile latency <= 500ms for 1k tokens.
- Key success criteria (from your side):
  1) Latency: 95th <= 500ms on representative traffic.
  2) Quality: summary ROUGE-L >= 0.68 on the provided benchmark set, and no more than 5% regression on taxonomy recall for aggressive edge cases.
  3) Cost: at least 30% reduction in token cost vs current baseline on equivalent throughput.

Proposed POC scope & timeline:
- Week 0 (this week): share evaluation template + data sample. Align on success criteria and owners.
- Week 1: Redwood devs provision dedicated sandbox, deploy model variant(s), run offline evals on sample dataset.
- Week 2: Shadow/online test with 10% traffic (non-production) for 48–72 hours; collect latency and quality metrics.
- Week 3: Final analysis, review, and decision point.

Ownership:
- Redwood: Marissa (PM lead) + Dylan (solutions eng) — infra setup, offline evals, shadow instrumentation.
- Acme: John (POC sponsor) + Priya (data lead) — provide dataset sample, define edge-case examples, run acceptance checks on results.

Next steps (action items):
1) John: share a 2–4k sample of anonymized customer interactions + any existing evaluation scripts by EOD Monday.
2) Marissa: send eval template + proposed offline tests (attached).
3) Dylan: schedule the 60-min kick-off for Monday or Tuesday to walk through the setup.

Attachments: acme-eval-template.xlsx, redwood-poc-setup-guide.pdf

If that all looks right, I'll send the calendar invite and kick off the infra provisioning.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — this matches our discussion. A couple of clarifications from our side: 

- Success criteria: the ROUGE-L target is fine, but we also need a manual spot-check rubric for hallucination/accuracy for top-100 high-risk cases. Priya will own that.
- Latency: 500ms 95th is OK for single-shot summarization; for multi-part aggregation flows we may need to measure end-to-end. We'll flag two representative flows in the dataset.
- Shadowing: we prefer an online shadow test (server-side copy) for 48 hours with sampling at 5–10% to avoid user impact. Is that feasible?

Timeline wise — we can get the anonymized sample and the edge-case list by Monday EOD. Can you confirm Redwood's expected data access method (S3, scp, or secure upload)? Also please share the evaluation template you mentioned.

John
VP Product, Acme Corp

Subject: Re: Acme POC - eval template, offline vs shadow plan, rubric

John / Priya —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Attached is the eval template (acme-eval-template.xlsx) and the Redwood POC setup guide. Below is a concrete proposal to align on methodology — offline evals vs online shadow — and the grading rubric so we can avoid last-minute scope creep.

1) Proposed hybrid eval approach (recommended):
  - Phase A (offline): run deterministic offline evals on your sample dataset. Purpose: fast feedback on model variants, reproducible quality metrics (ROUGE, BLEU, F1 where applicable), and automated edge-case scoring. Expected runtime: 24–48h.
  - Phase B (online shadow): server-side shadowing at 5% traffic for 48 hours on two representative flows. Purpose: validate latency under realistic load and surface any behavioral drift not captured offline (contextual prompts, session persistence).

2) Grading rubric (high level):
  - Quality (60%): ROUGE-L (weighted 30%), factual accuracy/manual spot checks (20%), hallucination rate on flagged cases (10%).
  - Latency (20%): 95th percentile, plus P99 as guardrail.
  - Cost efficiency (15%): projected per-token cost delta vs baseline under target throughput distribution.
  - Operational risk (5%): infra stability, error rate, and ability to scale to peak concurrency.

3) Data & access:
  - Preferred transfer: pre-signed S3 bucket. If not possible, secure upload to Redwood partner portal (we can create a temporary workspace).
  - We only need 2–4k anonymized interactions initially. For offline edge-case scoring, a separate CSV with 100 flagged examples is ideal.

4) Ownership & deliverables:
  - Redwood (Dylan): infra + instrumentation, offline eval scripts, metrics dashboard link, and final report.
  - Acme (Priya): dataset, ground truth labels for the 100 flagged examples, and acceptance decision.

5) Timeline (updated):
  - Tue (Day 0): dataset & flagged list delivered by Acme.
  - Wed–Thu: offline evals run, preliminary results shared.
  - Fri: online shadowing for 48h (Fri–Sat) with daily check-ins.
  - Next Mon: final sync to review outcomes and decision.

6) Quick asks / next steps:
  - John: confirm S3 transfer or request Redwood upload link.
  - Priya: confirm she'll own the manual spot checks and indicate which 100 examples to flag.
  - Dylan: if you can confirm infra ETA (sandbox ready by Wed) I'll schedule the offline job accordingly.

Attachments: redwood-poc-setup-guide.pdf, acme-eval-template.xlsx

Let me know if you'd prefer we run a longer shadow (72h) — we can accommodate but it will push the final sync back a day.

Best,
Marissa
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
